surfaces.part: open shelf compartments with bottles and boxes seen face-on

answer.evidence: The whole piece is a flat front view. The pale band at rows 1-6 is mottled and reads as a face-on header or glass panel. It has a 1-row divider line at row 7 but no eave shadow and no foreshortened depth. Rows 8-12 are a face-on sign panel with a green cross. Rows 14-28 show shelf compartments with their contents seen straight on, not from above, so there is no ellipse and no opening seen from above. The width is a constant 30 px from row 1 to row 31, so there are no receding planes. This is a cabinet front elevation, not a container with an opening.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 21 visible tones per tile, against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well, so it matches the richest references. Near-flat coverage is 11%, close to the stall's 13%, so there are no large flat fills beyond a few panel areas. None of its dark edge pixels are neutral (0%), so the outlines lean toward a dark tint of the neighbouring grey-blue material rather than a black sticker line. The cabinet body has about 4 lightness steps (pale face, door panels, shadowed frame, dark edge), a little below the references' 5-6. Shelf items, the green and red crosses, and bottle clusters add small-scale variation. Overall it is a plausible peer to the stall and well at the same scale, though the cabinet body is slightly less textured than the best references.
